Converged Route A magnitudes for catalogs v4.1 and v5.1

Decision D-B091 (PI, 2026-11-25 10:24). Branch analysis/mag-converged; large outputs in /wd1/mdenolle_data/magnitude_converged. Only the phase19 solver changed: amplitudes, SNR cut, station epochs, the Hutton-Boore distance term, the 150 km pick selection, the 4-MAD rejection, the ComCat ML anchors, the Mw switch at 4.5 and the Mw_cal rule are those of the stored runs.

Summary.
  • The phase19 inversion is now solved exactly: the 161,093 event terms are eliminated and the 1,338 station-phase terms come from a direct solve of their Schur complement, followed by two refinement steps. The last refinement step is 3e-13 and the relative normal-equation residual 2e-13. Two independent solvers agree with it: a sparse LU factorisation of the full normal equations (5e-7) and a column-scaled LSQR, which converges in about 330 iterations. One and twelve BLAS threads give the same ML to 1e-15.
  • The stored solver, LSQR stopped at 3000 iterations, is 0.07 from the minimum for the median event and 0.65 at the 99th percentile. It is not reproducible: 1 and 12 threads differ by up to 0.86 (99th percentile 0.075), and a rerun at 12 threads differs from the stored v4.1 file by up to 0.60.
  • v4.1 (the paper), converged minus stored ML, near events (median by region): Blanco -0.67, JdF ridge/plate -0.29, Gorda -0.19, Mendocino -0.19, offshore forearc -0.19, Endeavour +0.06, Explorer +0.01, Axial +0.07, onshore +0.005 to +0.014. v5.1 near events: Blanco -0.70, JdF -0.51, Gorda and Mendocino -0.29, offshore forearc -0.28, Explorer -0.08, Axial -0.06, onshore +0.01 to +0.015 (the D-B091 numbers); v5.1 moves more than v4.1 because its stored run had stopped further from the minimum. The 3,500 'mapped' events (recorded only beyond 150 km) drop by 0.2-0.45 everywhere, onshore included, because the Theil-Sen line that maps them is refitted to the new near ML.
  • With both catalogs converged, v5.1 minus v4.1 is +0.001 (stored pair +0.047) and -0.004 offshore (stored +0.070). The +0.07 offshore shift reported in the v5.1 magnitude piece was a solver artefact; only Axial keeps a real change (-0.24, from the relocation).
  • External references, v4.1: ComCat ML anchor gap at offshore and coastal labels +0.12 -> +0.01; anchor scatter 0.211 -> 0.174; tensor Mw 3-4.5 at offshore labels, near events, ML - Mw +0.11 -> -0.07 (v5.1 +0.26 -> -0.02).
  • Gauge: every ocean-bottom deployment is tied to the land network well enough that its formal level error is below 0.1 (most below 0.03). The stored offsets came from the solver, not from weak ties. The ties that are thin are NV 2014, 7A 2010, NV 2011 and OO 2014 (Axial). X9 (Blanco) has only 3-4 events with land picks; 3,800 events shared with 7D Y2, 401 with 7D Y3 and 108 with Z5 2013 carry its level. In phase19 the anchors set one global offset only; the cross-links set every deployment level. The northern California land network NC also moved, by +0.15 against the other land networks (v4.1). That is why Mendocino changes by -0.19 in every year, 2010-2011 included.
  • Mc (paper method, v4_mc_maps.py on v4.1): Blanco 2.2 -> 1.6, Gorda 2.1 -> 1.9, Mendocino triple junction 1.7 -> 1.5, Endeavour-Explorer 1.8 -> 1.6, offshore pooled 2.2 -> 1.7; onshore unchanged. The Blanco Mc 'improvement' between 2011-2012 and 2013-2015 (2.6 -> 2.2) disappears (1.5 -> 1.6), and the Blanco M >= 2.5 rate of 2010 and 2016 relative to 2013-2015 rises from 5% and 8% to 28% and 29%. The paper's Fig. 2, Figs. S3-S7, Table S6, the clustering (Figs. 5-6, Table S5) and about 30 numbers change (list in the last section).

1. Solver change and convergence proof

phase19 fits station ML = M_i + C_jp to the Hutton-Boore station magnitudes within 150 km, with two gauge rows (sum of the P terms = 0 and sum of the S terms = 0, row weight 1000) and damping 1e-3. The objective is unchanged. The stored runs solved it with LSQR stopped at 3000 iterations (istop 7). LSQR is slow on this system for two reasons. First, the column norms range from 1 (an event with one pick) to 130 (a station-phase term with 16,876 picks), and the gauge rows have weight 1000. Second, moving a whole deployment against its events changes the misfit little per unknown: the eigenvalue of that mode is the deployment's stiffness divided by its number of terms plus events (X9 0.25, Z5 2013 0.48, OO 2014 0.009, against 1.5e4 at the top of the data spectrum). Starting from zero station terms, LSQR resolves these modes last. Until it does, the large site terms of sediment-covered ocean-bottom stations stay in the event terms, so offshore ML comes out too high.

The new default, phase19_solver.solve(method='exact'), eliminates the event terms (their block of the normal equations is diagonal). The 1,338 x 1,338 Schur complement of the station terms is solved by a symmetric eigendecomposition, and two refinement steps follow on the full sparse system. It raises NotConverged unless the last refinement step is below 1e-8 and the relative normal-equation residual is below 1e-10. It also raises if any event with three or more picks sits in a part of the event / station graph that is not linked to the main network. There is one such isolated piece: the S term of 7D.J35C@2013-08-09 with 9 one-pick events, whose level is set by the damping only (stored value -234); none of its events has an ML. --solver lsqr runs a column-scaled LSQR with atol = btol = 1e-12 and fails unless istop is 1 or 2. --solver legacy3000 reproduces the stored runs.

With the phase19 tolerances LSQR reaches istop 2 after 4,591 iterations and is then still 0.064 from the minimum at the 99th percentile (largest 0.15). istop 2 bounds the gradient, not the error: in a soft direction the error is the gradient divided by a small eigenvalue. The D-B091 check (4,863 iterations on the stored v5.1 pick set) was therefore close, but not exact (section 4).

2. The gauge: how each ocean-bottom deployment is tied to the land network

Groups: every seafloor station-epoch, grouped by network and deployment year (7D = Cascadia Initiative years Y1-Y4); everything on land is the reference. Per group, on the final pick set of the converged run: n_events_with_land = events with picks on the group and on land stations; n_events_with_other_obs = events shared with another ocean-bottom group; n_anchors = ComCat ML anchors among its near events (dominated: anchors with at least half of their picks on the group); stiffness k = misfit increase per delta^2 when all its terms move by +delta and the events are re-fitted (the Schur complement; equal to the sum over events of n_G n_other / n, an effective number of tie picks); se_level = formal standard error of the mean term of the group minus the mean land term (sigma = 0.245, from the full inverse of the reduced system); dphi_opt_0.5 and dphi_naive_0.5 = misfit increase for delta = 0.5 with the events re-fitted, and with every event that has a pick on the group moved by -delta (the +delta/-delta test; total misfit 72,319); dC_minus_land = change of the mean term (converged minus stored) relative to the land mean; dML_dominated = median ML change of the events with at least half of their picks on the group; anchor_gap = median ML - ComCat ML of the dominated anchors.

The 7D sub-arrays (J, FN, FS, G, M per year) are in gauge_deployments.csv (level sub-array).

What the table shows:

  • No deployment is free. The largest formal error of a deployment level is 0.085-0.091 (NV 2014, 4 terms, 2 or fewer events with land picks); every other is 0.009-0.046. A 0.5 shift of a deployment costs from 2 (NV 2014) to 6,900 (7D Y4) in misfit, out of about 72,000.
  • Thin ties (stiffness below about 400): NV 2014 (k 8-10), 7A 2010 (69-75), NV 2011 (117-119; 0-2 events with land picks), OO 2014 (194-200; 66-71 of its 22,000 events have land picks), NV 2010 (244-256), NV 2013 (360-367) and 7D Y1 (376-406). Their levels rest on few links. OO 2014 carries the Axial catalog.
  • X9 2012 (Blanco) has only 3-4 events with land picks. It is tied through 3,800 events shared with 7D Y2, 401 with 7D Y3 and 108 with Z5 2013 (stiffness 5,300, s.e. 0.016); 7D Y2 in turn shares 2,615 events with land. It moved most (-0.67 to -0.71) because LSQR reaches this chain last, not because the data leave it free.
  • Anchors versus cross-links. In phase19 the 3,416 anchors (84% onshore) set one global offset and do not enter the deployment levels; the cross-links set every level. The anchors are an independent check. Where a deployment has 9 or more dominated anchors, convergence reduces the gap (v4.1): 7D Y2 +0.30 -> +0.03 (24 anchors), 7D Y4 +0.17 -> +0.02 (43), Z5 2013 +0.22 -> -0.09 (38), X9 +0.87 -> +0.23 (9); Z5 2014 stays at -0.12/-0.13 (13). OO 2014 (Axial) stays at +0.39/+0.40 with only 4 anchors; the 2 anchors in the Axial region are +0.9 above ComCat in both solutions. Axial is the one place where the anchors disagree with the cross-link level, and its ties are thin (open problem 1).
  • The land network is not one rigid block either. The northern California network NC (128 terms) moves by +0.15 (v4.1) and +0.25 (v5.1) against the other land networks, and BK by +0.10/+0.17. Events dominated by NC change by -0.17/-0.29. This is why Mendocino, Gorda and the offshore forearc change by the same -0.19 (v4.1) in every year, 2010 and 2011 included, when no ocean-bottom station was recording. NC is stiffly tied (s.e. 0.010; 21,030 events shared with the other land networks), so this too was the solver. Its 54 dominated anchors go from +0.39 to +0.24 above ComCat ML; the remaining +0.24 may be a scale difference between the NC local magnitudes in ComCat and the PNSN ones that dominate the anchor offset.

3. Catalog v4.1 (the paper's magnitudes)

New file /wd1/mdenolle_data/magnitude_converged/v4.1/cascadia_catalog_M_routeA_converged.csv (130,769 events, same columns and events as the stored data/magnitude_v4/cascadia_catalog_M_routeA.csv; the v4.1 patch is applied as in utils/fix_catalog_v4.py: 172113 removed, 900001-900003 copied from the stored file as ComCat Mw). Provenance: .provenance.json next to it (solver diagnostics of both passes, anchor offset and scatter, mapping fit, Mw_cal offsets, M_type counts, thread settings, MD5 of the stored and new files, git commit).

For near events at offshore labels with Mw 3-4.5, ML - Mw goes from +0.11 to -0.07 (v4.1) and from +0.26 to -0.02 (v5.1); onshore it stays at +0.05 to +0.12. Counted over all events, the offshore value goes to -0.21/-0.23 because of the 11-14 'mapped' tensor events: their ML comes from the Theil-Sen map of the inversion ML, whose slope fell from 1.15 to 1.01 when the near ML it is fitted to came down. phase19 already flags mapped ML above about 4 as lower bounds. Above Mw 4.5 the tensor Mw is used, so these values do not enter M.

D-B091 on the stored pick sets

On the pick set of the stored v5.1 run, the exact solver reproduces the D-B091 changes, and the D-B091 LSQR to istop 2 (4,863 iterations) is within 0.006 of it in every region except Axial (-0.03); its largest event error is 0.18. On the v4.1 pick set (the stored per-pick table was not kept, so a 12-thread legacy rerun stands in) the same LSQR is within 0.02 except Axial (+0.06). The data misfit drops by 274 (v5.1, 0.38%) and 184 (v4.1, 0.25%) from the stored to the exact solution. Redoing the first pass and the 4-MAD rejection with the exact solver changes only tens of picks per deployment and the regional medians by at most 0.02 (columns full_chain_minus_stored and rejection_effect). The larger Explorer and Endeavour changes in the all-event region tables come from the 'mapped' events (Explorer: 485 of 1,326), not from the rejection.

Offshore Mc drops by 0.2-0.6 with the magnitudes. With the paper's script (v4_mc_maps.py, mc_maps_v41/mc_regional.csv): Blanco 2.2 -> 1.6, Gorda 2.1 -> 1.9, Mendocino triple junction 1.7 -> 1.5, Endeavour-Explorer 1.8 -> 1.6, offshore pooled 2.2 -> 1.7. The Gorda value is borderline: GFT95 is reached at 1.9 there, but not in version A of v51_mc_b.py (the same events plus 3 duplicated rows of 900001-900003), which falls back to GFT90 = 1.7 with b 1.05 instead of 1.22. Onshore Mc does not change. Two period statements of the paper change. The Blanco Mc of 2011-2012 (2.6 stored) was inflated by the same deployment levels: converged it is 1.5, against 1.6 in 2013-2015, so the 'offshore Mc improved by 0.2-0.4 after the first two years' result does not hold (EN +0.1, BL -0.1, GO 0.0). The rate of M >= 2.5 Blanco events in 2010 and 2016, relative to 2013-2015, rises from 5% and 8% to 28% and 29%: the events of the ocean-bottom years came down by 0.6-0.7, those of 2010 and 2016 (mapped, land stations only) by about 0.3. The Mendocino 2016 ratio stays at 10-11%. b changes by -0.07 to +0.12 in the offshore boxes. In the onshore box (everything outside the named boxes) b goes from 0.92 to 1.01 although its median ML change is +0.01: 11% of its events drop by more than 0.1, half of them in northern California between 40 and 42 N (east of the triple-junction box, recorded by the Gorda and Mendocino ocean-bottom stations) and 12% of them 'mapped' events. Between converged v5.1 and converged v4.1 M (paired test, same events) b agrees within 0.03 in every box except Axial (+0.10 at Mc 0.1, the Axial relocation).

8. Files, reproduction, open problems

Code (branch analysis/mag-converged): workflow/05_magnitude/phase19_solver.py (new), phase19_preferred_magnitude.py (solver, --solver/--outdir/--tag, provenance), v51_magnitude_table.py (--pm/--out/--tag/--solver/--v4-mags), mag_converged.py (patch, near, threads, gauge, compare, reconcile, mcb), mag_converged_report.py and mag_converged_text.py (this page), scale/run_magnitude_converged.sh (driver). Resume notes: /wd1/mdenolle_data/magnitude_converged/RESUME.md.

Open problems

  1. Axial (OO 2014): converged ML is still +0.39 above ComCat ML on its 4 dominated anchors and +0.9 on the 2 anchors of the Axial region. The OO level rests on 66-71 events with land picks (stiffness about 200). Its level should be checked against the OOI/PNSN Axial catalogs before the Axial magnitudes are used for b or Mc.
  2. JdF ridge/plate and the 7D Y1/Y3 J stations: v4.1 near events move by -0.29 and v5.1 by -0.51, because the two stored runs stopped at different points; both converged runs agree (v5.1 - v4.1 = +0.005). The JdF plate has 4 ComCat anchors in total, so its level rests on the cross-links (7D Y1 stiffness about 400, s.e. 0.03) with no external check.
  3. The two gauge rows force the mean P term and the mean S term to be zero separately, which is one constraint more than the single null direction of the problem. It is kept (unchanged objective), but it makes the P-S level difference a fixed choice rather than a fitted one.
  4. 'Mapped' events (3,522 in v4.1) follow the Theil-Sen map fitted to the near events; the map changed (slope 1.15 -> 1.01), so mapped ML above about 3.5 dropped more than the region shift. Their tensor comparison (ML - Mw about -0.2 at Mw 3-4.5) is worse than before.
  5. The near-event Mw_cal offset rose from +0.04 to +0.19 (v4.1) because large offshore ML dropped while the tensors did not change; Mw_cal events: 35 -> 27. The ML - Mw shortfall above Mw 4.5 is larger (-0.79 -> -1.15 for all, -0.36 -> -0.69 for near events), which strengthens the case for the Mw switch.
  6. The converged v4.1 file is not placed next to the stored one in the main tree (other worktrees are not touched); the clustering rerun has no sensitivity variants; the paper figures 1, 3, 5, 6 and the atlas are not remade.
